def _spherical_point_in_cell(grid, y: np.ndarray, x: np.ndarray, yi: np.ndarray, xi: np.ndarray):
    """Check whether spherical points lie inside curvilinear grid cells.

    On a spherical mesh the cell corners are connected by great-circle arcs.
    Solving the inverse bilinear problem directly in longitude/latitude fails
    for cells that contain a geographic pole (for example the folded cells of
    tripolar ocean grids), because the bilinear interpolation of the corner
    longitudes/latitudes can never reach the pole itself.

    To handle such cells robustly, the corners and query points are first
    projected onto the plane tangent to the sphere at the cell centre using a
    gnomonic projection.  Great circles become straight lines in this
    projection, so the cell becomes a regular planar quadrilateral and the
    usual inverse bilinear solve applies.

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : XGrid
        The spherical curvilinear grid to search within.
    y, x : np.ndarray
        Latitudes and longitudes of the query points.
    yi, xi : np.ndarray
        Candidate cell indices for each query point.

    Returns
    -------
    xi_coord, eta_coord : np.ndarray
        Barycentric cell coordinates of the query points (-1 when the point
        is not inside the candidate cell).
    valid : np.ndarray of bool
        Whether each query point is inside its candidate cell.
    """
    n = len(yi)
    lon = grid.lon
    lat = grid.lat

    lonr = np.deg2rad(lon)
    latr = np.deg2rad(lat)
    cx0, cy0, cz0 = _latlon_rad_to_xyz(latr, lonr)

    # Cell corners in the order (00, 01, 11, 10).
    corner_x = np.stack(
        [
            cx0[yi, xi],
            cx0[yi, xi + 1],
            cx0[yi + 1, xi + 1],
            cx0[yi + 1, xi],
        ]
    )
    corner_y = np.stack(
        [
            cy0[yi, xi],
            cy0[yi, xi + 1],
            cy0[yi + 1, xi + 1],
            cy0[yi + 1, xi],
        ]
    )
    corner_z = np.stack(
        [
            cz0[yi, xi],
            cz0[yi, xi + 1],
            cz0[yi + 1, xi + 1],
            cz0[yi + 1, xi],
        ]
    )

    # Projection centre: mean of the corner unit vectors (normalised).
    centre = np.stack([corner_x.sum(axis=0), corner_y.sum(axis=0), corner_z.sum(axis=0)])
    centre_norm = np.linalg.norm(centre, axis=0)
    centre = centre / np.where(centre_norm > 0, centre_norm, 1.0)[np.newaxis, :]

    # Local orthonormal basis perpendicular to the projection centre.
    near_pole = np.abs(centre[2]) > 0.9
    aux = np.stack(
        [
            np.where(near_pole, 1.0, 0.0),
            np.zeros(n),
            np.where(near_pole, 0.0, 1.0),
        ]
    )
    e1 = np.cross(centre, aux, axis=0)
    e1_norm = np.linalg.norm(e1, axis=0)
    e1 = e1 / np.where(e1_norm > 0, e1_norm, 1.0)[np.newaxis, :]
    e2 = np.cross(centre, e1, axis=0)

    def _project(vx, vy, vz):
        denominators = vx * centre[0] + vy * centre[1] + vz * centre[2]
        tx = (vx * e1[0] + vy * e1[1] + vz * e1[2]) / denominators
        ty = (vx * e2[0] + vy * e2[1] + vz * e2[2]) / denominators
        return tx, ty, denominators

    px, py, corner_denominators = _project(corner_x, corner_y, corner_z)

    query_lat = np.deg2rad(y)
    query_lon = np.deg2rad(x)
    qx, qy, qz = _latlon_rad_to_xyz(query_lat, query_lon)
    point_x, point_y, query_denominators = _project(qx, qy, qz)

    # The gnomonic projection is only valid for points that lie in the
    # hemisphere centred on the projection centre.
    valid_projection = (
        (centre_norm > 1e-12)
        & np.all(corner_denominators > 0, axis=0)
        & (query_denominators > 0)
        & np.isfinite(point_x)
        & np.isfinite(point_y)
        & np.all(np.isfinite(px), axis=0)
        & np.all(np.isfinite(py), axis=0)
    )

    xi_coord, eta_coord, valid = _bilinear_inverse(px, py, point_x, point_y)
    valid &= valid_projection

    return xi_coord, eta_coord, valid


def curvilinear_point_in_cell(grid, y: np.ndarray, x: np.ndarray, yi: np.ndarray, xi: np.ndarray):
    px = np.array([grid.lon[yi, xi], grid.lon[yi, xi + 1], grid.lon[yi + 1, xi + 1], grid.lon[yi + 1, xi]])
    py = np.array([grid.lat[yi, xi], grid.lat[yi, xi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1, xi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1, xi]])

    xsi = eta = -1.0 * np.ones(px.shape[1], dtype=float)

    if grid._mesh == "spherical":
        # Map grid and particle longitudes to [-180,180)
        px = ((px + 180.0) % 360.0) - 180.0
        x_wrapped = ((x + 180.0) % 360.0) - 180.0

        # Create a mask for antimeridian cells
        lon_span = px.max(axis=0) - px.min(axis=0)
        antimeridian_cell = lon_span > 180.0

        if np.any(antimeridian_cell):
            # For any antimeridian cell ...
            #  If particle longitude is closer to 180.0, then negative cell longitudes need to be bumped by +360
            mask = (px < 0.0) & antimeridian_cell[np.newaxis, :] & (x_wrapped[np.newaxis, :] > 0.0)
            px[mask] += 360.0
            #  If particle longitude is closer to -180.0, then positive cell longitudes need to be bumped by -360
            mask = (px > 0.0) & antimeridian_cell[np.newaxis, :] & (x_wrapped[np.newaxis, :] < 0.0)
            px[mask] -= 360.0
    else:
        x_wrapped = x

    xsi, eta, found = _bilinear_inverse(px, py, x_wrapped, y)

    # On spherical meshes the longitude/latitude formulation breaks down for
    # cells that contain a geographic pole (e.g. tripolar fold cells).  Fall
    # back to a gnomonic projection for points that were not located.
    if grid._mesh == "spherical" and np.any(~found):
        n = px.shape[1]
        y_broadcast = np.broadcast_to(y, (n,))
        x_broadcast = np.broadcast_to(x, (n,))
        missing = np.flatnonzero(~found)
        xi_f, eta_f, found_f = _spherical_point_in_cell(
            grid, y_broadcast[missing], x_broadcast[missing], yi[missing], xi[missing]
        )
        xsi[missing] = np.where(found_f, xi_f, xsi[missing])
        eta[missing] = np.where(found_f, eta_f, eta[missing])
        found[missing] |= found_f

    is_in_cell = np.where(found, 1, 0)

    return is_in_cell, np.column_stack((xsi, eta))

def _gnomonic_cell_coordinates(grid, yi, xi):
    """Project spherical cell corners onto a local tangent plane.

    The projection centre is the normalised mean of the four corner unit
    vectors and the projection is gnomonic (great circles map to straight
    lines).

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : XGrid
        The spherical grid.
    yi, xi : np.ndarray
        Cell indices for which the projection is requested.

    Returns
    -------
    px, py : np.ndarray
        Planar coordinates of the four cell corners (shape ``(4, n)``).
    centre : np.ndarray
        Unit vector pointing to the projection centre (shape ``(3, n)``).
    e1, e2 : np.ndarray
        Orthonormal basis vectors of the tangent plane (shape ``(3, n)``).
    valid : np.ndarray of bool
        Whether the projection is well defined for each cell.
    """
    n = len(yi)
    lonr = np.deg2rad(grid.lon)
    latr = np.deg2rad(grid.lat)
    cx0, cy0, cz0 = _latlon_rad_to_xyz(latr, lonr)

    # Cell corners in the order (00, 01, 11, 10).
    corner_x = np.stack(
        [
            cx0[yi, xi],
            cx0[yi, xi + 1],
            cx0[yi + 1, xi + 1],
            cx0[yi + 1, xi],
        ]
    )
    corner_y = np.stack(
        [
            cy0[yi, xi],
            cy0[yi, xi + 1],
            cy0[yi + 1, xi + 1],
            cy0[yi + 1, xi],
        ]
    )
    corner_z = np.stack(
        [
            cz0[yi, xi],
            cz0[yi, xi + 1],
            cz0[yi + 1, xi + 1],
            cz0[yi + 1, xi],
        ]
    )

    # Projection centre: mean of the corner unit vectors (normalised).
    centre = np.stack([corner_x.sum(axis=0), corner_y.sum(axis=0), corner_z.sum(axis=0)])
    centre_norm = np.linalg.norm(centre, axis=0)
    valid_centre = centre_norm > 1e-12
    centre = centre / np.where(valid_centre, centre_norm, 1.0)[np.newaxis, :]

    # Local orthonormal basis perpendicular to the projection centre.
    near_pole = np.abs(centre[2]) > 0.9
    aux = np.stack(
        [
            np.where(near_pole, 1.0, 0.0),
            np.zeros(n),
            np.where(near_pole, 0.0, 1.0),
        ]
    )
    e1 = np.cross(centre, aux, axis=0)
    e1_norm = np.linalg.norm(e1, axis=0)
    valid_basis = e1_norm > 1e-12
    e1 = e1 / np.where(valid_basis, e1_norm, 1.0)[np.newaxis, :]
    e2 = np.cross(centre, e1, axis=0)

    valid = valid_centre & valid_basis

    denominators = corner_x * centre[0] + corner_y * centre[1] + corner_z * centre[2]
    px = (corner_x * e1[0] + corner_y * e1[1] + corner_z * e1[2]) / denominators
    py = (corner_x * e2[0] + corner_y * e2[1] + corner_z * e2[2]) / denominators
    valid &= np.all(denominators > 0, axis=0) & np.all(np.isfinite(px), axis=0) & np.all(np.isfinite(py), axis=0)

    return px, py, centre, e1, e2, valid


def _project_to_tangent_plane(vectors, centre, e1, e2):
    """Project 3-D unit vectors onto the tangent plane defined by ``centre``."""
    denominators = vectors[0] * centre[0] + vectors[1] * centre[1] + vectors[2] * centre[2]
    tx = (vectors[0] * e1[0] + vectors[1] * e1[1] + vectors[2] * e1[2]) / denominators
    ty = (vectors[0] * e2[0] + vectors[1] * e2[1] + vectors[2] * e2[2]) / denominators
    return tx, ty, denominators


def _pole_cells(grid):
    """Return a boolean array marking cells whose geometry contains a pole.

    For such cells (for example the folded cells of tripolar ocean grids) the
    bilinear interpolation of the corner longitudes/latitudes does not
    represent the actual cell on the sphere, so the longitude/latitude search
    has to be replaced by the tangent-plane formulation.
    """
    ny, nx = grid.lon.shape
    yi = np.repeat(np.arange(ny - 1), nx - 1)
    xi = np.tile(np.arange(nx - 1), ny - 1)

    px, py, centre, e1, e2, valid = _gnomonic_cell_coordinates(grid, yi, xi)

    flagged = np.zeros(len(yi), dtype=bool)
    for pole in (np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), np.array([0.0, 0.0, -1.0])):
        pole_vector = np.broadcast_to(pole[:, np.newaxis], (3, len(yi)))
        pole_x, pole_y, denominators = _project_to_tangent_plane(pole_vector, centre, e1, e2)
        # A loose tolerance catches poles that lie exactly on a cell edge.
        _, _, pole_in_cell = _bilinear_inverse(px, py, pole_x, pole_y, tol=5e-2)
        flagged |= pole_in_cell & valid & np.all(denominators > 0, axis=0)

    return flagged.reshape((ny - 1, nx - 1))


def _spherical_point_in_cell(grid, y: np.ndarray, x: np.ndarray, yi: np.ndarray, xi: np.ndarray):
    """Check whether spherical points lie inside curvilinear grid cells.

    On a spherical mesh the cell corners are connected by great-circle arcs.
    Solving the inverse bilinear problem directly in longitude/latitude fails
    for cells that contain a geographic pole (for example the folded cells of
    tripolar ocean grids), because the bilinear interpolation of the corner
    longitudes/latitudes can never reach the pole itself.

    To handle such cells robustly, the corners and query points are first
    projected onto the plane tangent to the sphere at the cell centre using a
    gnomonic projection.  Great circles become straight lines in this
    projection, so the cell becomes a regular planar quadrilateral and the
    usual inverse bilinear solve applies.

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : XGrid
        The spherical curvilinear grid to search within.
    y, x : np.ndarray
        Latitudes and longitudes of the query points.
    yi, xi : np.ndarray
        Candidate cell indices for each query point.

    Returns
    -------
    xi_coord, eta_coord : np.ndarray
        Barycentric cell coordinates of the query points (-1 when the point
        is not inside the candidate cell).
    valid : np.ndarray of bool
        Whether each query point is inside its candidate cell.
    """
    px, py, centre, e1, e2, valid_projection = _gnomonic_cell_coordinates(grid, yi, xi)

    query_lat = np.deg2rad(y)
    query_lon = np.deg2rad(x)
    qx, qy, qz = _latlon_rad_to_xyz(query_lat, query_lon)
    point_x, point_y, query_denominators = _project_to_tangent_plane(
        np.stack([qx, qy, qz]), centre, e1, e2
    )

    # The gnomonic projection is only valid for points that lie in the
    # hemisphere centred on the projection centre.
    valid_projection &= (query_denominators > 0) & np.isfinite(point_x) & np.isfinite(point_y)

    xi_coord, eta_coord, valid = _bilinear_inverse(px, py, point_x, point_y)
    valid &= valid_projection

    return xi_coord, eta_coord, valid


def curvilinear_point_in_cell(grid, y: np.ndarray, x: np.ndarray, yi: np.ndarray, xi: np.ndarray):
    px = np.array([grid.lon[yi, xi], grid.lon[yi, xi + 1], grid.lon[yi + 1, xi + 1], grid.lon[yi + 1, xi]])
    py = np.array([grid.lat[yi, xi], grid.lat[yi, xi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1, xi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1, xi]])

    xsi = eta = -1.0 * np.ones(px.shape[1], dtype=float)

    if grid._mesh == "spherical":
        # Map grid and particle longitudes to [-180,180)
        px = ((px + 180.0) % 360.0) - 180.0
        x_wrapped = ((x + 180.0) % 360.0) - 180.0

        # Create a mask for antimeridian cells
        lon_span = px.max(axis=0) - px.min(axis=0)
        antimeridian_cell = lon_span > 180.0

        if np.any(antimeridian_cell):
            # For any antimeridian cell ...
            #  If particle longitude is closer to 180.0, then negative cell longitudes need to be bumped by +360
            mask = (px < 0.0) & antimeridian_cell[np.newaxis, :] & (x_wrapped[np.newaxis, :] > 0.0)
            px[mask] += 360.0
            #  If particle longitude is closer to -180.0, then positive cell longitudes need to be bumped by -360
            mask = (px > 0.0) & antimeridian_cell[np.newaxis, :] & (x_wrapped[np.newaxis, :] < 0.0)
            px[mask] -= 360.0
    else:
        x_wrapped = x

    xsi, eta, found = _bilinear_inverse(px, py, x_wrapped, y)

    if grid._mesh == "spherical":

        # represented by the bilinear lon/lat patch: their lon/lat formulation

        # that belong to neighbouring cells.  For those cells, and as a
        # fallback for any point that the lon/lat formulation could not
        # locate, use the tangent-plane (gnomonic) formulation.
        pole_cells = getattr(grid, "_pole_cells", None)
        if pole_cells is None:

        polar_candidate = pole_cells[yi, xi]

        if np.any(polar_candidate | ~found):

            eta[needs_spherical] = np.where(use_spherical, eta_f, eta[needs_spherical])
            found[needs_spherical] = np.where(use_spherical, found_f, found[needs_spherical])

ny, nx = lon.shape

    data_vars={'observation': (('y','x'), field_values)},
    coords={'x': ('x', np.arange(nx), {'axis':'X'}),
            'y': ('y', np.arange(ny), {'axis':'Y'}),

)

def curvilinear_point_in_cell(grid, y: np.ndarray, x: np.ndarray, yi: np.ndarray, xi: np.ndarray):
    px = np.array([grid.lon[yi, xi], grid.lon[yi, xi + 1], grid.lon[yi + 1, xi + 1], grid.lon[yi + 1, xi]])
    py = np.array([grid.lat[yi, xi], grid.lat[yi, xi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1, xi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1, xi]])

    xsi = eta = -1.0 * np.ones(px.shape[1], dtype=float)

    if grid._mesh == "spherical":
        # On a spherical mesh the cell edges are great-circle arcs.  Solving
        # the inverse bilinear problem directly in longitude/latitude is not
        # reliable for such cells: it can neither reach points inside cells
        # that contain a geographic pole (e.g. the folded cells of tripolar
        # ocean grids) nor represent cells whose longitude span crosses the
        # antimeridian.  The corners and query points are therefore projected
        # onto the plane tangent to the sphere at each cell centre (gnomonic
        # projection), where the cell becomes a regular planar quadrilateral.
        n = px.shape[1]
        y_broadcast = np.broadcast_to(y, (n,))
        x_broadcast = np.broadcast_to(x, (n,))
        xsi, eta, found = _spherical_point_in_cell(grid, y_broadcast, x_broadcast, yi, xi)

        # Fall back to the lon/lat formulation for degenerate cells whose
        # tangent-plane projection is not well defined.
        if np.any(~found):
            px = ((px + 180.0) % 360.0) - 180.0
            x_wrapped = ((x + 180.0) % 360.0) - 180.0

            # Create a mask for antimeridian cells
            lon_span = px.max(axis=0) - px.min(axis=0)
            antimeridian_cell = lon_span > 180.0

            if np.any(antimeridian_cell):
                # For any antimeridian cell ...
                #  If particle longitude is closer to 180.0, then negative cell longitudes need to be bumped by +360
                mask = (px < 0.0) & antimeridian_cell[np.newaxis, :] & (x_wrapped[np.newaxis, :] > 0.0)
                px[mask] += 360.0
                #  If particle longitude is closer to -180.0, then positive cell longitudes need to be bumped by -360
                mask = (px > 0.0) & antimeridian_cell[np.newaxis, :] & (x_wrapped[np.newaxis, :] < 0.0)
                px[mask] -= 360.0

            xsi_ll, eta_ll, found_ll = _bilinear_inverse(px, py, x_wrapped, y)
            missing = ~found
            xsi[missing] = np.where(found_ll[missing], xsi_ll[missing], xsi[missing])
            eta[missing] = np.where(found_ll[missing], eta_ll[missing], eta[missing])
            found[missing] |= found_ll[missing]
    else:

    is_in_cell = np.where(found, 1, 0)

    return is_in_cell, np.column_stack((xsi, eta))

def _pole_cells(grid):
    """Return a boolean array marking cells whose geometry contains a pole.

    For such cells (for example the folded cells of tripolar ocean grids) the
    bilinear interpolation of the corner longitudes/latitudes does not
    represent the actual cell on the sphere, so the longitude/latitude search
    has to be replaced by the tangent-plane formulation.
    """
    ny, nx = grid.lon.shape
    yi = np.repeat(np.arange(ny - 1), nx - 1)
    xi = np.tile(np.arange(nx - 1), ny - 1)

    px, py, centre, e1, e2, valid = _gnomonic_cell_coordinates(grid, yi, xi)

    flagged = np.zeros(len(yi), dtype=bool)
    for pole in (np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), np.array([0.0, 0.0, -1.0])):
        pole_vector = np.broadcast_to(pole[:, np.newaxis], (3, len(yi)))
        pole_x, pole_y, denominators = _project_to_tangent_plane(pole_vector, centre, e1, e2)
        # A loose tolerance catches poles that lie exactly on a cell edge.
        _, _, pole_in_cell = _bilinear_inverse(px, py, pole_x, pole_y, tol=5e-2)
        flagged |= pole_in_cell & valid & (denominators > 0)

    return flagged.reshape((ny - 1, nx - 1))

94	def _bilinear_inverse(px, py, x, y, tol=1e-9):
95	    """Solve the inverse bilinear problem for vectorised query points.
96	
97	    The bilinear mapping is
98	
99	        X(xi, eta) = a0 + a1 * xi + a2 * eta + a3 * xi * eta
100	        Y(xi, eta) = b0 + b1 * xi + b2 * eta + b3 * xi * eta
101	
102	    with ``a = invA @ px`` and ``b = invA @ py``, where ``px`` and ``py``
103	    contain the four cell corners in the order (00, 01, 11, 10).
104	
105	    Both roots of the resulting quadratic equation in ``eta`` are
106	    considered and the first solution whose ``(xi, eta)`` pair lies inside
107	    the unit cell is returned.
108	
109	    Parameters
110	    ----------
111	    px, py : np.ndarray
112	        Corner coordinates with shape ``(4, n)``.
113	    x, y : np.ndarray
114	        Query point coordinates with shape ``(n,)``.
115	    tol : float
116	        Tolerance used when checking whether the solution lies in [0, 1].
117	
118	    Returns
119	    -------
120	    xi, eta : np.ndarray
121	        The barycentric cell coordinates, set to -1 for points for which no
122	        valid solution exists.
123	    valid : np.ndarray of bool
124	        Whether a solution inside the cell was found.
125	    """
126	    invA = np.array(
127	        [
128	            [1, 0, 0, 0],
129	            [-1, 1, 0, 0],
130	            [-1, 0, 0, 1],
131	            [1, -1, 1, -1],
132	        ]
133	    )
134	
135	    n = px.shape[1]
136	    a = np.dot(invA, px)
137	    b = np.dot(invA, py)
138	
139	    aa = a[3] * b[2] - a[2] * b[3]
140	    bb = a[3] * b[0] - a[0] * b[3] + a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1] + x * b[3] - y * a[3]
141	    cc = a[1] * b[0] - a[0] * b[1] + x * b[1] - y * a[1]
142	    det2 = bb * bb - 4 * aa * cc
143	
144	    xi = np.full(n, -1.0)
145	    eta = np.full(n, -1.0)
146	    valid = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
147	
148	    # Quadratic equation is (numerically) linear when aa is negligible.
149	    linear = np.abs(aa) < 1e-12
150	    has_real_roots = np.where(linear, np.abs(bb) > 1e-30, det2 >= 0)
151	
152	    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore", over="ignore"):
153	        det = np.sqrt(np.where(det2 > 0, det2, 0.0))
154	
155	        # Candidate solutions for eta.  Rows are the two quadratic roots and
156	        # the linear fallback; only rows that are meaningful for each point
157	        # are considered below.
158	        candidates = np.stack(
159	            [
160	                np.where(linear, -cc / bb, (-bb + det) / (2 * aa)),
161	                np.where(linear, -cc / bb, (-bb - det) / (2 * aa)),
162	            ]
163	        )
164	
165	        for eta_candidate in candidates:
166	            eta_test = np.where(has_real_roots & np.isfinite(eta_candidate), eta_candidate, np.nan)
167	
168	            denominator = a[1] + a[3] * eta_test
169	            # Fallback used for cells whose sides are parallel to the y-axis.
170	            xi_test = np.where(
171	                np.abs(denominator) < 1e-12,
172	                ((y - py[0]) / (py[1] - py[0]) + (y - py[3]) / (py[2] - py[3])) * 0.5,
173	                (x - a[0] - a[2] * eta_test) / denominator,
174	            )
175	
176	            is_valid = (
177	                has_real_roots
178	                & np.isfinite(xi_test)
179	                & np.isfinite(eta_test)
180	                & (xi_test >= -tol)
181	                & (xi_test <= 1 + tol)
182	                & (eta_test >= -tol)
183	                & (eta_test <= 1 + tol)

187	            eta = np.where(is_valid, np.clip(eta_test, 0.0, 1.0), eta)

193	def _gnomonic_cell_coordinates(grid, yi, xi):
194	    """Project spherical cell corners onto a local tangent plane.
195	
196	    The projection centre is the normalised mean of the four corner unit
197	    vectors and the projection is gnomonic (great circles map to straight
198	    lines).
199	
200	    Parameters
201	    ----------
202	    grid : XGrid
203	        The spherical grid.
204	    yi, xi : np.ndarray
205	        Cell indices for which the projection is requested.
206	
207	    Returns
208	    -------
209	    px, py : np.ndarray
210	        Planar coordinates of the four cell corners (shape ``(4, n)``).
211	    centre : np.ndarray
212	        Unit vector pointing to the projection centre (shape ``(3, n)``).
213	    e1, e2 : np.ndarray
214	        Orthonormal basis vectors of the tangent plane (shape ``(3, n)``).
215	    valid : np.ndarray of bool
216	        Whether the projection is well defined for each cell.
217	    """
218	    n = len(yi)
219	    lonr = np.deg2rad(grid.lon)
220	    latr = np.deg2rad(grid.lat)
221	    cx0, cy0, cz0 = _latlon_rad_to_xyz(latr, lonr)
222	
223	    # Cell corners in the order (00, 01, 11, 10).
224	    corner_x = np.stack(
225	        [
226	            cx0[yi, xi],
227	            cx0[yi, xi + 1],
228	            cx0[yi + 1, xi + 1],
229	            cx0[yi + 1, xi],
230	        ]
231	    )
232	    corner_y = np.stack(
233	        [
234	            cy0[yi, xi],
235	            cy0[yi, xi + 1],
236	            cy0[yi + 1, xi + 1],
237	            cy0[yi + 1, xi],
238	        ]
239	    )
240	    corner_z = np.stack(
241	        [
242	            cz0[yi, xi],
243	            cz0[yi, xi + 1],
244	            cz0[yi + 1, xi + 1],
245	            cz0[yi + 1, xi],
246	        ]
247	    )
248	
249	    # Projection centre: mean of the corner unit vectors (normalised).
250	    centre = np.stack([corner_x.sum(axis=0), corner_y.sum(axis=0), corner_z.sum(axis=0)])
251	    centre_norm = np.linalg.norm(centre, axis=0)
252	    valid_centre = centre_norm > 1e-12
253	    centre = centre / np.where(valid_centre, centre_norm, 1.0)[np.newaxis, :]
254	
255	    # Local orthonormal basis perpendicular to the projection centre.
256	    near_pole = np.abs(centre[2]) > 0.9
257	    aux = np.stack(
258	        [
259	            np.where(near_pole, 1.0, 0.0),
260	            np.zeros(n),
261	            np.where(near_pole, 0.0, 1.0),
262	        ]
263	    )
264	    e1 = np.cross(centre, aux, axis=0)

266	    valid_basis = e1_norm > 1e-12
267	    e1 = e1 / np.where(valid_basis, e1_norm, 1.0)[np.newaxis, :]
268	    e2 = np.cross(centre, e1, axis=0)

270	    valid = valid_centre & valid_basis

272	    denominators = corner_x * centre[0] + corner_y * centre[1] + corner_z * centre[2]
273	    px = (corner_x * e1[0] + corner_y * e1[1] + corner_z * e1[2]) / denominators
274	    py = (corner_x * e2[0] + corner_y * e2[1] + corner_z * e2[2]) / denominators
275	    valid &= np.all(denominators > 0, axis=0) & np.all(np.isfinite(px), axis=0) & np.all(np.isfinite(py), axis=0)

+    centre : np.ndarray

+    e1, e2 : np.ndarray

+    valid : np.ndarray of bool

+    corner_lon = np.stack(
